scope: Cumulative R43 R40+R34 compiler with a new inline singleton sample fastpath inside AggregateFunctionTimeseriesBase.h for all timeSeries*ToGrid derived functions. Keep original hash map and serialization wire format for 0,2+ samples or merged/deserialized dense states. Exact direct one-bucket/one-sample state avoids any hash allocation per series. No storage, query, tags, index, R36/R39/R41/R42 changes.
hypothesis: On sparse CI-shaped native queries with 1 sample per series, bucket-map allocation per aggregate state is avoidable. Hold one (bucket index,timestamp,value) in the aggregate state; spill to the existing R34 hash map on second sample. Native full 1.33m/14d can reduce memory and CPU beyond R43 without changing semantics or on-disk layout.
baseline: R43 cumulative R40+R34 optimized build (under construction), same LLVM22.1.8 Release O2 jemalloc
candidate: R44 = R43 plus reversible one-sample inline storage in AggregateFunctionTimeseriesBase.h; no other changes
guards: All native 160 cases against R43, including NaN/Inf/stale, duplicate timestamps, offsets, subquery, multi metric error and group-by variants
dense 8192 series ×256 samples at 15s, independent analytic rate oracle with resets/out-of-order cases
Single-sample and dense aggregate state same serialization version bytes; deserialize/merge fallback works
Check spillage same bucket and different bucket, key 0, single/zero samples, parallel merges
A/B/B/A same frozen 1.33m series/14d RAW_UUID and cgroup limits; negative latency controls
falsifier: Compile/link failure, any native oracle or serialization mismatch, large regression on dense selectors, or no repeatable memory+CPU win beyond R43
runner_budget: One R43-cached O2 binary, native guards and matched 4-phase same host benchmark. Require R43 gates before promotion.
